title: Per-vertex scalar attribute + gradient shader (infra)
description:
Context: patch-diagnostic work needs to visualize continuous per-vertex scalar fields (e.g. Coons reconstruction error, Gaussian curvature, mean dihedral). Today HalfEdgeMeshRuntime only supports per-tag uniform solidColor. A patch rendered with one color per-patch hides intra-patch variation — critical for Coons error since the whole point is to see WHERE inside a patch reconstruction fails.

This ticket adds a reusable pipeline. Callers push a float[] vertex-count-long; GPU interpolates across the triangle; fragment shader maps scalar to a dark→bright ramp. The infra ticket produces no user-visible change on its own — it unblocks the Coons-error metric (see sibling ticket) and any other per-vertex scalar diagnostic.

Proposed additions:
- `ixdar-app/src/main/resources/glsl/mesh_scalar.vs` / `mesh_scalar.fs` — new shader pair. Vertex declares `layout(location=3) in float aScalar;` (position/normal/texcoord at 0/1/2 stay as-is). Vertex writes `vScalar = aScalar;` varying. Fragment maps v = clamp(vScalar, 0, 1) to color via a cheap ramp — e.g. `color = vec3(v, v * 0.7, 0.2 + 0.3 * v)` for a dark-red→bright-yellow warm scale, or `vec3(v)` for pure grayscale. Start with grayscale so "dark = low, bright = high" matches the user's spec literally.
- `ShaderProgram.ShaderType` — add `MeshScalar` entry pointing at the new files.
- `HalfEdgeMeshRuntime` — new field `int scalarVbo`, new attribute slot, new method `setPerVertexScalar(float[] values)` that uploads and sets the VBO to active. A new ShaderMode entry `SCALAR` (or folded into whichever diagnostic consumes it).
- `PatchRenderer.renderSingleView` / `renderSingleViewWithOverlay` — extend to optionally take a `float[] vertexScalar` and do barycentric-interpolated grayscale per pixel so the CPU PNG diagnostic matches the GL view. Reuse the existing triangle rasterizer's barycentric weights.

The Coons-error ticket (PATCH-16) will call `setPerVertexScalar(errorArray)` with per-vertex error values and pick this shader via a new ShaderMode.

Critical files to modify / create:
- ixdar-app/src/main/resources/glsl/mesh_scalar.vs (new)
- ixdar-app/src/main/resources/glsl/mesh_scalar.fs (new)
- ixdar-app/src/main/java/ixdar/graphics/render/shaders/ShaderProgram.java
- ixdar-app/src/main/java/ixdar/graphics/render/model/HalfEdgeMeshRuntime.java (lines 25-80 for new state, 131-206 for render path, 290+ for setters)
- ixdar-app/src/main/java/ixdar/geometry/mesh/data/PatchRenderer.java (renderSingleView)
definition-of-done:
1. A new shader program `MeshScalar` loads at runtime alongside `Mesh` and `MeshUnlit`.
2. `HalfEdgeMeshRuntime.setPerVertexScalar(float[])` uploads a per-vertex float buffer; the GL path binds it when a scalar-aware ShaderMode is active.
3. Values are interpolated across triangles and mapped dark→bright in a fragment shader (grayscale baseline).
4. `PatchRenderer.renderSingleView` has an overload that accepts a `float[] vertexScalar` and produces the same dark→bright shading in CPU PNG output.
5. A trivial smoke test drives this with a synthetic scalar field (e.g. vertex-index modulo N normalized to [0,1]) and confirms both GL view and CPU PNG show a smooth gradient.
testing-plan:
1. Live viewer: load a mesh, activate the new SCALAR ShaderMode with a synthetic gradient (vertex y-coordinate normalized to [0,1]). Confirm smooth gradient across faces, no flat-shaded discontinuities at triangle edges.
2. CPU PNG: call renderSingleView with the same synthetic scalar on voyage_skull_ref.obj. Read the output — should show smooth gradient.
3. Regression: LAMBERT, FLAT, STAGES, CREST_VS_BOUNDARY modes still render identically to before.
